title: Polyglot SDK: Resumable fragment streams with function-call provenance and schema-anchored bindings
creator: Lina Park
description: Introduce a reference implementation and migration guide for SDKs (TypeScript/Python/Go) that supports resumable fragment streaming, explicit function/tool-call provenance, and schema-anchored structured output bindings. The aim is to give application teams a single interoperable pattern for: 1) resuming partially-delivered streaming responses mid-session, 2) recording exact tool/function call metadata for observability and replay, and 3) mapping incremental fragments to typed output objects validated against a shared JSON-schema. This ticket produces: reference interfaces, cross-language examples, test harness, compatibility shim layer, and a short migration playbook for customers currently using older streaming shims.
acceptance_criteria: TS/py/go SDKs expose a minimal session object capable of start/resume/commit/abort flows
Every streamed fragment is emitted with provenance metadata (request_id, call_id, tool_name, offset, checksum)
Structured fragments can be reassembled and validated against a provided JSON-Schema, producing a typed object in each language
A shim is provided that maps existing non-resumable streaming APIs to the new sessioned API with <= 10ms added latency in microbenchmarks
Comprehensive end-to-end tests: unit tests for fragment reassembly and integration tests with runtime (mocked) for failures and retries
Migration guide and one example GitHub PR demonstrating conversion of a sample app from legacy streaming to the new pattern
notes: Background: internal compat work is fragmented across multiple ad-hoc SDK patterns; customers ask for deterministic replay and observability of tool calls.
We want to avoid a heavy RPC layer. Keep wire format as compact framed JSON events similar to existing stream envelopes but add a small header for provenance.

Tradeoffs: adding resumability requires lightweight persistent state (session manifest). We will implement a pluggable storage interface with an in-memory default, Redis/DB-backed adapters for Dedicated/Private.
Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Sessioned+Streaming+RFC (internal) — keep examples minimal and idiomatic per language.
Performance target: end-to-end P95 additional latency < 15ms for typical small fragments; added memory per active session < 2KB average.

sample_py_interface:
# Python: simple resumable session abstraction
from typing import Callable, TypedDict

class FragmentMeta(TypedDict):
    request_id: str
    call_id: str
    tool: str
    offset: int
    checksum: str

class FragmentChunk(TypedDict):
    meta: FragmentMeta
    payload: str
    is_final: bool

class ResumableSession:
    def __init__(self, id: str):
        self.id = id
    def start(self, schema_url: str | None = None) -> None: ...
    def on_fragment(self, cb: Callable[[FragmentChunk], None]) -> None: ...
    def resume(self, manifest_token: str) -> None: ...
    def commit(self) -> str: ...
    def abort(self, reason: str | None = None) -> None: ...

migration_notes: Migration playbook (high level): 1) Identify endpoints using legacy streaming; add lightweight adapter that wraps existing event stream and emits framed FragmentChunk events. 2) Add session manifest persistence (in-memory for dev, Redis for Dedicated). 3) Generate typed bindings from canonical JSON-Schema and wire them into SDK examples. 4) Update server-side runtime to emit provenance headers (request_id, call_id, tool) — backward-compatible: servers can continue emitting previous envelopes and adapter will fill missing provenance with best-effort tokens. 5) Run integration tests with simulated disconnects; tune retry/backoff policy. 6) Rollout can be gradual per-route; provide a canary toggle in Console and a metric dashboard for resume_success_rate, avg_resume_latency, fragment_validation_errors.
qa_plan: Unit tests for fragment checksum and offset ordering
Property tests for random partial deliveries and reassembly correctness
Integration test connecting SDK to runtime mock that simulates network partitions and tool failures
Performance microbenchmarks across TS/Py/Go clients; memory/latency targets must be met
Manual end-to-end verification with sample app (chat-with-tools) and Console toggles
